metadata.title: LT: How to Request a 401(k) Termination Cash Withdrawal or Rollover
metadata.description: Guide a former employee through requesting a termination distribution from a ForUsAll-administered 401(k), including cash withdrawal, rollover, or a split transaction, using the participant portal or the RightSignature electronic form. The form link is always shared together with the portal steps as a secondary option, clearly labeled to be used only if the participant has problems with the website or cannot log in (for example, MFA is not enrolled). Covers delivery methods and fees, including OverNight Check delivery, which can only be requested on the RightSignature electronic form and is not available in the participant portal. Includes intent-scoped rollover best practices such as correct wire vs. check details, data-entry tips, and common errors to avoid. This article is specific to the recordkeeper LT Trust.

rules: The participant must have a Terminated status & Termination date in the system.
Only vested balances are eligible for distribution.
If there is a Rehire date in the system, the Termination date must be after or higher than the Rehire date.
Not mentioned from the Plan Data, that the plan is in a Blackout period.
The Participant must have MFA enrolled for participant portal access.

Select Separation of Service if the participant has already left their employer. If the portal shows 'Default' instead of Separation of Service due to a website issue, the participant should select Default and continue because it is the same option.
If the participant is still employed and wants to roll over eligible funds (such as rollover source balances), they must contact ForUsAll Support first to confirm eligibility.
A $75 distribution fee applies to all requests.
For a cash distribution, no additional delivery charge applies for ACH or Regular Mail Check. ACH is cash-only and must not be presented as a rollover delivery method.
An additional $35 wire fee applies if a wire is chosen.

An additional $50 OverNight Check fee applies if an OverNight Check is chosen. OverNight Check can only be requested on the RightSignature electronic form, so this fee only applies to form requests. Do not mention the OverNight Check option or the $50 OverNight Check fee when explaining the participant portal (website) process.
Wire transfer and OverNight Check fees are non-refundable.
For a cash distribution or the cash portion of a split transaction, 20% federal MANDATORY withholding applies.
State withholding may also apply to the cash or cash portion (subject to the state's tax laws).
Cash distributions are taxable income for the calendar year processed. Cash withholding does not apply to a direct rollover.
Submitting through the participant portal is the preferred and fastest route.

Always include the RightSignature electronic form link in the response alongside the portal steps, and state clearly that the form should be used only if the participant is having problems with the website or cannot log in (for example, MFA is not enrolled). Form link: https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723. Share this link only after termination distribution eligibility is confirmed (Terminated status and termination date on file). Do not ask the participant to contact Support just to obtain the form.
The RightSignature electronic form is a slower secondary option and must never be presented as the default or preferred route while the participant can use the portal.
OverNight Check delivery can only be requested on the RightSignature electronic form; it cannot be selected in the participant portal.
Checks are sent via USPS or UPS.
Wires require exact instructions to avoid rejections and returns.
A returned wire or rejected ACH may be converted to a mailed check sent to the participant's home address on file.
Overnight checks are sent via UPS and cannot be delivered to P.O. boxes; a physical street address is required.

OverNight Check cannot be selected in the participant portal. A participant who wants an overnight check must submit the request on the RightSignature electronic form, where the additional $50 OverNight Check fee applies.
Participants must go to forusall.com/login and use their credentials to log in.
Participants access the rollover or distribution flow by selecting Loans & Distributions from the dashboard.
Best practices: use a computer or laptop (not mobile) and use an up-to-date browser (Chrome or Edge recommended).
The participant must select a payment method for rollovers: check or wire.
ACH is not a rollover delivery method; do not include ACH in a pure direct-rollover response.
The participant should confirm with their receiving provider how they prefer to receive rollovers (check or wire) before submitting.
Rollover destination options include IRA, Qualified Plan, Roth IRA, and Roth Qualified Plan.
Traditional funds can be rolled over into a Traditional type account or a Roth type account (Roth conversion may have tax implications), and Roth funds must be rolled over into a Roth type account.
Many financial institutions have different instructions for wires versus ACH; participants must use wire-specific details when selecting a wire transfer.
Incorrect wire instructions may cause funds to be rejected and reissued by check, adding delays.
Participants should verify wire details directly with the receiving institution before submitting.

Each wire transaction is subject to an extra $35 non-refundable fee charged by American Trust. If pre-tax and Roth sources require separate wire transactions, disclose the $35 fee for each separate wire/source.

For wire rollovers, the participant must provide: Bank account name, ABA routing number, bank account number, subaccount number (such as the IRA or Roth IRA account number), and the financial institution that receives the wire on behalf of the provider.

For check rollovers, participants must provide the receiving institution and a mailing address (either the receiving institution address or the participant address if they want the check mailed to them directly).
If the participant selects IRA or Roth IRA as the rollover destination, they must include the account number for that IRA.
Rollover destination options include IRA, Qualified Plan, Roth IRA, and Roth Qualified Plan.
Some fields (such as financial institution name or address) have system-imposed character limits; participants may need abbreviated names or addresses to avoid rejections or manual corrections.
Do not include 'FBO [Your Name]' in the Financial Institution field; it will automatically appear in the paperwork.
If the provider accepts rollovers via wire, confirm the participant is using the provider's wire-specific routing and account numbers.
Wire transfers are typically completed within 1–2 weeks.
Overnight check transfers are typically completed within 1–2 weeks.
Standard checks usually arrive within 2–3 weeks via USPS.

When a participant asks to cash out after leaving employment but no termination date is on file, ask only for their termination date (last day of employment); do not ask for payment details while eligibility is still blocked.

After Terminated status and the termination date are confirmed, present two submission paths: the participant portal under Loans & Distributions as the primary path, plus the secure RightSignature form as a fallback only for website/login problems: https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723.
Before a rollover, confirm with the receiving provider that it accepts the source type and whether it requires check or wire delivery.
Use the participant portal path: log in, select Loans & Distributions, select Separation of Service (or Default if that is the displayed equivalent), and start Termination Distribution.
Always include the RightSignature form as a secondary fallback after the portal path when eligibility is confirmed; use it only for website/login problems.
ForUsAll reviews the request within about two business days; after approval, wires typically complete in 1–2 weeks and standard checks in 2–3 weeks.
The participant receives Form 1099-R by January 31 of the following year for a rollover or cash distribution.
If an outstanding loan exists, direct the participant to Support to review repayment and possible tax consequences before submission.
Wait at least 7 business days after final payroll before submitting so pending contributions are included.

If Crypto Enrollment is active or the participant mentions crypto-window holdings, do not assume or promise how those holdings will transfer or be liquidated; contact ForUsAll Support before submission because this article does not define that operational treatment.
If a participant has an outstanding 401(k) loan at the time of the termination distribution, they may repay the loan in full to avoid taxes and penalties on the loan balance.

If the outstanding loan is not repaid, the remaining loan balance will be treated as a taxable distribution (subject to federal income tax, and state income taxes may also apply depending on the participant's state of residence) and may also incur an additional 10% IRS early withdrawal penalty if the participant is under 59 1/2.
Participants should contact ForUsAll Support to discuss loan repayment options before initiating the distribution request.

This article primarily covers OUTGOING rollovers (moving funds out of the ForUsAll plan). The flow for INCOMING rollovers (bringing funds from a previous employer's 401(k) or another qualified plan INTO the ForUsAll plan) is the inverse and is initiated by the participant on the SENDING institution's side, not in the ForUsAll portal.

To roll over a 401(k) from a prior employer into the ForUsAll plan, the participant must contact the prior recordkeeper (the one currently holding the old 401(k)) and request an outgoing rollover/distribution from THAT recordkeeper, payable to the ForUsAll plan FBO (for the benefit of) the participant.

The participant should provide the prior recordkeeper with the ForUsAll receiving instructions: plan name, ForUsAll's mailing address for rollover checks (or wire instructions if supported), the participant's name, and the participant's ForUsAll account/SSN as required.
Once the funds arrive at ForUsAll, the participant should notify ForUsAll Support so the incoming rollover can be matched to their account and invested per their election.
Incoming rollovers from a Roth 401(k) or Roth IRA must be kept in Roth source; pre-tax rollovers go to the pre-tax source. Mixing sources is not allowed.

The 60-day indirect rollover rule applies if the prior recordkeeper sends the funds to the participant first rather than directly to ForUsAll: the participant has 60 days from receipt to deposit the funds into the ForUsAll plan, or the distribution is taxable.

If the participant explicitly states they have separated from employment (resigned, quit, were fired or laid off, no longer work here, or are a former employee), treat this as a separation claim even if the system Eligibility Status still shows 'Active'.

When a separation claim conflicts with an 'Active' system status, do NOT offer hardship withdrawal, 401(k) loan, or in-service distribution — these are available only to actively employed participants. An 'Active' status alongside an explicit separation claim most likely means the admin system has not been updated yet.

In this conflict: (1) ask the participant for their termination/separation date; (2) tell them we will review this internally because the system still shows them as active; (3) escalate to the team to verify and update the employment status.

fees.notes: Applies in addition to the Distribution request fee if a wire is chosen; non-refundable.

Applies in addition to the Distribution request fee if an OverNight Check is chosen; non-refundable. OverNight Check can only be requested on the RightSignature electronic form, not in the participant portal, so this fee never applies to a request submitted through the website.

steps.description: The participant must log in to the ForUsAll 401(k) participant portal and open the 'Loans & Distributions' area from the dashboard.
steps.notes: Portal submission is the fastest route. The participant must log in at https://account.forusall.com/login. Best practices: use a computer or laptop (not mobile) and use an up-to-date browser (Chrome or Edge recommended). Always share the RightSignature electronic form link together with these portal steps (after confirming eligibility), telling the participant to use it only if they run into problems on the website or cannot log in, for example because MFA is not enrolled: https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723

steps.description: The participant must select a distribution reason for the request.
steps.notes: The participant must choose Separation of Service. If Separation of Service is unavailable or the portal shows 'Default' instead due to a website issue, the participant must choose Default and continue because it is the same option.

steps.description: The participant must review account sources and vesting before continuing.
steps.notes: The portal shows Traditional and any Roth sources and vesting percentages. Only vested balances are eligible. If vesting looks incorrect, the participant must contact ForUsAll Support before submitting.

steps.description: The participant must enter email confirmation information.
steps.notes: The participant must expand Email Confirmation Information and enter at least one valid email address for updates or inquiries.

steps.description: The participant must choose the distribution type and how funds will be delivered.
steps.notes: The participant must choose from the following options: lump sum cash distribution, a direct rollover of my vested balance to an IRA or a Qualified Retirement Plan, or partial direct rollover to an IRA or qualified plan with the remaining balance as a cash distribution.

steps.description: The participant must provide delivery details for the chosen option.
steps.notes: For cash requests, the participant may choose check, ACH, or wire and must provide the matching delivery details; cash-only withholding applies. For rollover checks, the participant must provide the receiving institution, mailing address, rollover destination type (IRA, Qualified Plan, Roth IRA, or Roth Qualified Plan), and the IRA or sub-account number if selecting IRA or Roth IRA. For rollover wires, the participant must provide the bank account name, ABA routing number, bank account number, subaccount number (such as the IRA or Roth IRA account number), and the financial institution that receives the wire on behalf of the provider. ACH must never be offered for a direct rollover. Important: many financial institutions have different instructions for wires versus ACH — the participant must use wire-specific details. Do not include 'FBO [Your Name]' in the Financial Institution field; it will automatically appear in the paperwork. Some fields have system-imposed character limits; participants may need to abbreviate names or addresses. OverNight Check is not offered in the portal. A participant who needs an overnight check must submit the request on the RightSignature electronic form instead, where an additional $50 OverNight Check fee applies.

steps.description: The participant must review elections and submit the request in the portal.
steps.notes: The participant must confirm the elections that apply to the selected transaction and then submit. For cash or a cash portion, review tax withholding and delivery. For a direct rollover, review the receiving account type and check/wire instructions; do not add cash withholding. Traditional funds can go into a Traditional type account or a Roth type account (Roth conversion may have tax implications), and Roth funds must go into a Roth type account.

steps.description: The participant must track review, processing, and delivery timelines after submission.
steps.notes: ForUsAll reviews within about two business days. Standard checks typically arrive in about 2–3 weeks after approval via USPS. Wires typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval depending on the receiving institution. Overnight checks (available only on the RightSignature electronic form) typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval.

common_issues.issue: Cannot log in or access the participant portal due to Participant data 'MFA' is 'not enrolled'.
common_issues.resolution: MFA is required for participant portal access. If the participant cannot access the portal because MFA is not enrolled, provide them directly with the RightSignature electronic form to proceed with the distribution request (share it only after confirming termination distribution eligibility): https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723. If the participant prefers to use the portal, they must create an online account using the email on file and enroll MFA by going to the portal login URL, clicking on 'New here? Create an Account' and following the instructions.

common_issues.issue: The participant cannot log in or access the participant portal and Participant data 'MFA' is 'enrolled' (Participant doesn't mention they have forgotten their password).
common_issues.resolution: If MFA status is enrolled, the participant has already set up an authenticator app on their cellphone (for example Okta Verify or Google Authenticator). Remind the participant to locate their authenticator app, retrieve the current code, and enter it when prompted. If the participant confirms they do not have access to the authenticator app, it is not working, or they cannot find it, they must call the Participant Support team at '844-401-2253' to verify their identity and reset their MFA.

common_issues.issue: The participant cannot log in or access the participant portal due to Participant have forgotten their password.
common_issues.resolution: The participant must use the portal login URL provided in references, click on 'Forgot your password?' and follow the instructions to reset their password. The participant must be advised that they must use the email on file to correctly reset their password. If the participant mentions they are not getting the password reset email, advise them to check their spam/junk folder. If they still cannot locate it, they must contact Participant Support team at '844-401-2253', business hours Monday to Friday 7AM to 5PM PST for further assistance.

common_issues.issue: The participant cannot log in or access the participant portal due to error '10051' or any other error code.
common_issues.resolution: Advise the participant to contact ForUsAll Support to confirm their account information.

common_issues.issue: The Participant mentions that the Separation of Service reason is not listed.
common_issues.resolution: If the portal displays Default as the equivalent separation reason, the participant may select Default and proceed. If neither Separation of Service nor Default appears, or separation status is uncertain, the participant must contact ForUsAll Support.

common_issues.issue: The Participant mentions that the Account Balance is 0.
common_issues.resolution: The Participant must contact ForUsAll Support.

common_issues.issue: The Participant mentions that the Vesting percentage appears incorrect.
common_issues.resolution: Do not submit the distribution request yet. Contact ForUsAll Support to review vesting records before proceeding.

common_issues.issue: Check or Wire not received after the expected timeframe.
common_issues.resolution: Allow about 2–3 weeks from approval for check processing and delivery times, and 1–2 weeks for wires. If overdue, the Participant must contact ForUsAll Support.

common_issues.issue: The Participant is unsure about taxes for a cash distribution.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that 20% federal withholding applies and state withholding may also apply, and that the distribution is taxable income for the calendar year processed. Recommend consulting a tax professional for personal circumstances.

common_issues.issue: Loans & Distributions section does not load in the portal.
common_issues.resolution: Have the participant refresh the browser or clear the cache before retrying. Best practices: use a computer or laptop (not mobile) and use an up-to-date browser (Chrome or Edge recommended).

common_issues.issue: Receiving institution name or address exceeds system character limits during rollover submission.
common_issues.resolution: Advise the participant to confirm with the receiving provider whether abbreviations are acceptable for long names or addresses.

common_issues.issue: Incorrect wire routing or account numbers entered (using ACH details instead of wire-specific details).
common_issues.resolution: Advise the participant to obtain and use wire-specific routing and account numbers from the receiving provider and verify accuracy before submitting. Many financial institutions have different instructions for wires versus ACH.

common_issues.issue: Wire rejected by receiving institution and reissued by check.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that incorrect wire instructions caused rejection and reissue by check. The extra wire fee is non-refundable, so the participant should confirm all wire details with the receiving institution before submitting.

common_issues.issue: The participant selected overnight check on the RightSignature electronic form but provided a P.O. box as the mailing address.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that overnight checks are sent via UPS, which does not deliver to P.O. boxes. The participant must provide a physical street address for overnight delivery. Remember that overnight check delivery is only available on the RightSignature electronic form and carries an additional $50 non-refundable fee.

common_issues.issue: The participant mentions they are not receiving the authentication code through their emails or text messages, and Participant data 'MFA' is 'enrolled' (Participant doesn't mention they have forgotten their password).
common_issues.resolution: Clarify that the code is generated by the authenticator app on their cellphone they set up when they created the ForUsAll online account (for example Okta Verify or Google Authenticator). If the participant confirms they do not have the code, the code is not working, they got a new phone, or they no longer have access to the app, the participant must call the Participant Support team at '844-401-2253', business hours Monday to Friday 7AM to 5PM PST to verify their identity and reset their MFA code.

common_issues.issue: The Participant mentions that the Account Total Vested Balance is $0.
common_issues.resolution: The Participant must contact ForUsAll Support.

common_issues.issue: The Participant mentions that the Account Balance is empty or listed as '--'.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that this most likely means the current Total Vested Balance is $0.00 due to no contributions registered or the balance was already moved. The Participant must contact ForUsAll Support to confirm.

common_issues.issue: The Participant mentions that there are 2 different balances shown in their account — one higher at the top left, and another one in the 'Total Vested Balance' section.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that the balance at the top may include employer contributions that are not yet vested. The Total Vested Balance is the amount that is fully vested and available for distribution. The Participant must contact ForUsAll Support for clarification on non-vested balances.

common_issues.issue: The Participant asks why they cannot take the full amount shown at the top left corner of the dashboard.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that the balance at the top may include employer contributions that are not yet vested. The Total Vested Balance is the amount that is fully vested and available for distribution. The Participant must contact ForUsAll Support for clarification on non-vested balances.

common_issues.issue: I have a vested balance and want to take the money out, but I can't find where to initiate the process online.
common_issues.resolution: Restate the portal steps: log in at forusall.com/login, go to Loans & Distributions at the top right, in the Separation of Service section click the drop down and select Termination Distribution (or Default if Termination Distribution is not visible), then Get Started at the bottom, choose the distribution method (check/wire/rollover), and submit the request for review and processing. If the participant still cannot locate it or cannot log in, advise contacting ForUsAll Support.

common_issues.issue: Participant's balance dropped to $0 and they believe it was an error.
common_issues.resolution: Do not infer why the balance changed. Direct the participant to ForUsAll Support to review the transaction history and account status.

common_issues.issue: Participant is trying to submit a termination distribution but is not terminated or does not have a termination date on file.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that the participant can initiate a termination distribution request only if they are terminated and have a termination date on file. The participant can either wait until they have a termination date updated if the termination date was recently added, or if the termination date will be in a near future, or contact their employer to request them to update the termination date through their payroll system. Once the employer updates the termination date on their payroll, we will update it as well.

common_issues.issue: The participant submitted a termination distribution request too soon after their last paycheck and some contributions are missing.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that submitting before all contributions are processed can result in missing funds. A second distribution request (with a second $75 fee) may be needed to collect the remaining balance. Advise waiting at least 7 business days after the final paycheck before submitting.

common_issues.issue: The participant has an outstanding 401(k) loan and wants to request a termination distribution.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that the participant may repay the outstanding loan in full before initiating the distribution to avoid taxes and penalties on the loan balance. If the loan is not repaid, the remaining loan balance will be treated as a taxable distribution (subject to federal income tax, and state income taxes may also apply depending on the participant's state of residence) and may also incur an additional 10% IRS early withdrawal penalty if the participant is under 59 1/2. Advise the participant to contact ForUsAll Support to discuss loan repayment options before initiating the distribution request.

common_issues.issue: The participant has already tried the common troubleshooting steps and is still experiencing issues or the issue mentioned is not listed in the common issues.
common_issues.resolution: Advise the participant to contact ForUsAll Support to resolve the issue.

common_issues.issue: The participant's system status shows Active, but they explicitly state they have already separated from employment (resigned, quit, or were terminated).
common_issues.resolution: Do not proceed with an active-employee-only option (hardship, loan, or in-service distribution). Ask for the participant's termination/separation date, explain that the system still shows them as active and that we will review this internally to update their employment status, and escalate to ForUsAll Support with the stated separation date. Once the termination date is on file, the termination distribution process can proceed.

common_issues.issue: The participant is submitting through the portal and asks for an overnight check.
common_issues.resolution: Explain that an overnight check cannot be selected in the participant portal and can only be requested on the RightSignature electronic form. After confirming eligibility, share the form and disclose the additional $50 non-refundable OverNight Check fee on top of the $75 distribution fee: https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723

examples.scenario: Participant wants a taxable cash payout to a personal bank via wire.
examples.outcome: Use Lump Sum Cash Distribution with wire delivery. Provide complete bank routing and account details and a mailing address. Expect a $75 distribution fee plus a $35 wire fee, and 20% federal withholding (plus any applicable state withholding).

examples.scenario: Participant wants to roll 100% to a Traditional IRA at their IRA provider.
examples.outcome: Use Full Rollover with check or wire delivery. If using a wire, list the receiving institution as the bank account name and include routing and account details and the IRA sub-account number. If a wire returns, a rollover check may be mailed instead.

examples.scenario: Participant wants to split 60% to an IRA and 40% as cash.
examples.outcome: Use Partial Rollover plus Partial Cash and provide delivery instructions for each portion by percentage or dollar amount, including separate check or wire details as needed.

examples.scenario: Vesting shows 80% but the participant expected 100%.
examples.outcome: Do not proceed with submission until vesting is reviewed. Only vested amounts are eligible, so the participant should contact ForUsAll Support to review vesting.

examples.scenario: Participant is wiring rollover funds to their IRA provider and is unsure which bank details to use.
examples.outcome: Advise the participant to obtain wire-specific routing and account details from the receiving institution, including any intermediary bank details if provided, and verify the details directly with the receiving institution before submitting. Do not use ACH details for wire transfers.

examples.scenario: Participant selected check as rollover payment method and wants the funds sent immediately to their IRA provider.
examples.outcome: Advise the participant to wait the standard 2–3 weeks for USPS delivery after approval, as the processing time by the custodian cannot be modified.

examples.scenario: A participant with a Terminated status and a termination date on file has an account Total Vested Balance of $250 and wants to roll the funds into another retirement plan.
examples.outcome: The participant can proceed with a standard termination distribution request in the ForUsAll portal. Refer to the rollover best practices in this article for how to proceed.

examples.scenario: A participant states their Total Vested Balance shows as '--'.
examples.outcome: Explain that this most likely means the current Total Vested Balance is $0.00. To confirm, the participant must contact ForUsAll Support.

examples.scenario: A participant with a Terminated status and a termination date on file has MFA enrolled, has online access, and does not know how to request a distribution.
examples.outcome: Restate the navigation steps (log in > Loans & Distributions > Separation of Service section > select Termination Distribution or Default). If the participant still cannot locate it, advise them to contact ForUsAll Support for assistance.

examples.scenario: A participant with a Terminated status and a termination date on file has an account Total Vested Balance of $500 and wants a paper check as a cash lump sum distribution.
examples.outcome: The participant can proceed with a standard termination distribution request in the ForUsAll portal if they have MFA enrolled and can log in: log in, go to Loans & Distributions, in the Separation of Service section select Termination Distribution (or Default if not visible), then choose Lump Sum and check as the method, and submit the request. Also share the RightSignature electronic form link in the same response, telling them to use it only if they have problems on the website or cannot log in (for example, MFA is not enrolled): https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723

examples.scenario: A participant with a Terminated status and a termination date on file has an account Total Vested Balance of $1,200 and wants a wire transaction as a lump sum distribution.
examples.outcome: The participant can proceed with a standard termination distribution request in the ForUsAll portal if they have MFA enrolled and can log in: log in, go to Loans & Distributions, in the Separation of Service section select Termination Distribution (or Default if not visible), then choose wire as the method, and submit the request. Also share the RightSignature electronic form link in the same response, telling them to use it only if they have problems on the website or cannot log in (for example, MFA is not enrolled): https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723

examples.scenario: A participant asks how to get their distribution check overnighted.
examples.outcome: Explain that overnight check delivery cannot be selected in the participant portal and must be requested on the RightSignature electronic form, and that an additional $50 non-refundable OverNight Check fee applies on top of the $75 distribution fee. Overnight checks are sent via UPS and require a physical street address, not a P.O. box.

Checks typically arrive in about 2–3 weeks after approval via USPS.
Wires typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval depending on the receiving institution.
Overnight checks, which are only available on the RightSignature electronic form, typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval depending on the receiving institution.
A $75 distribution fee applies to all requests.
An additional $35 non-refundable fee applies to each separate wire transaction; separate pre-tax and Roth wires each incur the fee.

An additional $50 fee applies if an OverNight Check is chosen and is non-refundable. OverNight Check is only available on the RightSignature electronic form, so this fee is never quoted for a portal request.
For cash distributions or the cash portion of a split request, 20% mandatory federal withholding applies and state withholding may also apply; this does not apply to a direct rollover.
Cash distributions are taxable income for the calendar year processed.
The participant will receive an IRS Form 1099-R by January 31 of the following year for tax reporting purposes. This applies to both cash distributions and rollovers.
An additional 10% early withdrawal penalty may apply to a taxable cash amount if the participant is under 59 1/2 years old; do not include this in a pure direct-rollover response.
The portal displays Traditional and any Roth sources.
Ensure the receiving account accepts the tax character of the funds (for example, Roth IRA for Roth amounts).
Traditional funds can be rolled over into a Traditional type account or a Roth type account (Roth conversion may have tax implications), and Roth funds must be rolled over into a Roth type account.

Always share the RightSignature electronic form link together with the portal instructions (after eligibility is confirmed), and state clearly that the participant should use it only if they have problems with the website or cannot log in, for example because MFA is not enrolled. The form is typically slower than portal submission. Form link: https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723
OverNight Check delivery is only available on the RightSignature electronic form and adds a $50 non-refundable fee; it cannot be selected in the participant portal.

Direction: this is the INCOMING rollover flow — bringing money from a previous employer's 401(k) into the participant's ForUsAll 401(k). It is the opposite of the outgoing rollover flow that the rest of this article describes.

Step 1 — Contact the prior recordkeeper: the participant must call or log in to the recordkeeper that holds the old 401(k) and request a rollover distribution. ForUsAll cannot initiate this from its portal because ForUsAll is the RECEIVING plan, not the holder of the funds.

Step 2 — Choose direct vs indirect rollover: direct rollover (recommended) — the prior recordkeeper sends funds directly to ForUsAll, no taxes withheld. Indirect rollover — the participant receives the funds personally and has 60 days to deposit them into ForUsAll or the distribution becomes taxable.

Step 3 — Provide ForUsAll receiving instructions: the participant gives the prior recordkeeper the ForUsAll plan name, the FBO (for benefit of) participant designation, and the mailing/wire instructions provided by ForUsAll Support.

Step 4 — Notify ForUsAll once funds are in transit: the participant should email or call ForUsAll Support with the expected amount, source institution, and tax character (Roth vs pre-tax) so the rollover can be matched to their account when it arrives.
Step 5 — Confirm allocation: once posted, the participant should verify the rollover appears in their ForUsAll account and is invested per their current election.

Source preservation: Roth funds from the prior plan must come in as Roth source; pre-tax funds must come in as pre-tax source. The prior recordkeeper's distribution paperwork will indicate which source each portion is from.
Some fields (such as financial institution name or address) have system-imposed character limits; participants may need abbreviated names or addresses.
Do not include 'FBO [Your Name]' in the Financial Institution field; it will automatically appear in the paperwork.
If the provider accepts rollovers via wire, confirm the participant is using the provider's wire-specific routing and account numbers, not ACH details.

faq_pairs.question: Where do the funds go in a termination distribution or rollover?
faq_pairs.answer: Funds move from the ForUsAll plan out to the participant or another institution as a distribution or outgoing rollover.

faq_pairs.question: What should I do if Separation of Service is not available as a reason?
faq_pairs.answer: If the portal displays Default as the equivalent separation reason, select Default and proceed. If neither Separation of Service nor Default appears, or separation status is uncertain, contact ForUsAll Support.

faq_pairs.question: What are the delivery timelines for checks and wires?
faq_pairs.answer: ForUsAll reviews within about two business days. Standard checks typically arrive in about 2–3 weeks after approval via USPS, wires typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval depending on the receiving institution, and overnight checks (available only on the RightSignature electronic form) typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval.

faq_pairs.question: How long does a rollover approval typically take?
faq_pairs.answer: ForUsAll reviews the rollover request and supporting paperwork within about two business days after submission. Once approved, the funds are released to the receiving institution: wires typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval, overnight checks (available only on the RightSignature electronic form) also typically complete in about 1–2 weeks after approval, and standard USPS checks typically arrive in about 2–3 weeks after approval. The approval review itself (two business days) is separate from the delivery time.

faq_pairs.question: What taxes apply to a cash distribution?
faq_pairs.answer: A 20% federal withholding applies and state withholding may also apply. The distribution is taxable income for the calendar year processed.

faq_pairs.question: Will ForUsAll help complete all required fields on this form?
faq_pairs.answer: No. While this is a ForUsAll form, certain required fields must be completed using information provided directly by the other financial institution. ForUsAll is unable to supply or verify information that must come from an external company. If you're unsure what information is needed, we recommend contacting the advisor or representative at the other institution so they can provide the correct details for you to enter on the form or request.

faq_pairs.question: Im gonna left my employer in a future date, can I request a distribution now?
faq_pairs.answer: No, you can't request a distribution now. You must have a termination date in our system to request a distribution.

faq_pairs.question: Im gonna left my employer in a future date, what options do I have?
faq_pairs.answer: Once you have a termination date, you can: request a full cash distribution, request a full rollover, or request a partial rollover plus partial cash.

faq_pairs.question: Where does the participant start the rollover process online?
faq_pairs.answer: The participant logs in at forusall.com/login, then selects Loans & Distributions from the dashboard and chooses Separation of Service under Termination Distribution.

faq_pairs.question: How do I roll over my old employer's 401(k) into my ForUsAll plan?
faq_pairs.answer: This is an INCOMING rollover (the opposite of the outgoing flow this article mostly describes). The participant initiates it by contacting the prior recordkeeper (the institution holding the old 401(k)) and requesting a rollover distribution payable to the ForUsAll plan FBO (for the benefit of) the participant. A direct rollover — funds sent straight from the prior recordkeeper to ForUsAll — is recommended to avoid the 60-day indirect-rollover risk. The participant should also notify ForUsAll Support with the expected amount, source institution, and tax character (Roth vs pre-tax) so the incoming funds can be matched to the account once they arrive.

faq_pairs.question: What information does the prior recordkeeper need to send funds to ForUsAll?
faq_pairs.answer: The prior recordkeeper needs the ForUsAll plan name, FBO designation (for benefit of [participant name]), and ForUsAll's mailing address for rollover checks (or wire instructions if the prior recordkeeper supports outgoing wires). Contact ForUsAll Support to obtain the current receiving instructions; they may include a specific mailing PO box, plan ID, and the participant's account number or SSN as required.

faq_pairs.question: What should a participant do if they are still employed but want to roll over eligible funds?
faq_pairs.answer: Contact ForUsAll Support to confirm eligibility.

faq_pairs.question: What information is required for rollovers by wire?
faq_pairs.answer: Bank account name, ABA routing number, bank account number, subaccount number (such as the IRA or Roth IRA account number), and the financial institution that receives the wire on behalf of the provider. The participant must use wire-specific details, not ACH details.

faq_pairs.question: What information is required for rollovers by check?
faq_pairs.answer: Financial institution, mailing address, and rollover destination type (IRA, Qualified Plan, Roth IRA, or Roth Qualified Plan). If IRA or Roth IRA is selected, the participant must include the IRA account number.

faq_pairs.question: Can a participant request help submitting a distribution request without doing it online?
faq_pairs.answer: Yes. The RightSignature electronic form link is shared in the response together with the portal steps, with a clear note that it should be used only if the participant has problems with the website or cannot log in (for example, MFA is not enrolled): https://secure.rightsignature.com/templates/105723c3-eaf1-4a44-aaed-09ad5c253ec8/template-signer-link/a9d83fbb137e5315fbd641bb522b9723. For security reasons, participants must complete the form themselves, and Support cannot initiate the request for them.

faq_pairs.question: How can a participant get additional assistance if they need help with a distribution request?
faq_pairs.answer: They can contact ForUsAll Support by email at 'help@forusall.com' or by phone at 844-401-2253. Business hours Monday to Friday 7 am to 5 pm PT (Closed on national Holidays).

faq_pairs.question: My Total Vested Balance shows as '--'. What does this mean?
faq_pairs.answer: This most likely means the current Total Vested Balance is $0.00 or the balance was already moved. To confirm, please contact ForUsAll Support.

faq_pairs.question: What happens to my outstanding 401(k) loan if I request a termination distribution?
faq_pairs.answer: You may repay the loan in full before initiating the distribution to avoid taxes and penalties on the loan balance. If the loan is not repaid, the remaining loan balance will be treated as a taxable distribution and may also incur an additional 10% IRS early withdrawal penalty if you are under 59 1/2. Contact ForUsAll Support to discuss loan repayment options before initiating your distribution request.

faq_pairs.question: Will I receive a tax form for my distribution or rollover?
faq_pairs.answer: Yes, you will receive an IRS Form 1099-R by January 31 of the following year for tax reporting purposes. This applies to both cash distributions and rollovers.

faq_pairs.question: Can a participant request an overnight check through the website?
faq_pairs.answer: No. The participant portal only offers check, ACH, and wire delivery. An overnight check can only be requested on the RightSignature electronic form, and it carries an additional $50 non-refundable fee on top of the $75 distribution fee.

faq_pairs.question: How much is the overnight check fee?
faq_pairs.answer: The OverNight Check fee is $50 and is non-refundable. It applies in addition to the $75 distribution fee, and only to requests submitted on the RightSignature electronic form, because overnight delivery cannot be selected in the participant portal. The wire fee is a separate $35 fee.

definitions.definition: A distribution reason used when a participant has left their employer and is requesting a termination distribution.
A payment to the participant that is taxable and subject to required withholding.
A distribution type where funds are transferred to another qualified retirement account, such as an IRA or a new employer's 401(k), instead of being paid directly to the participant.
Transfers the participant's entire account balance to another qualified retirement account.
Transfers part of the participant's balance to another qualified retirement account and distributes the remaining balance as cash.

In a 401(k), being vested means the participant has earned the legal right to keep employer contributions (and their earnings) even if they leave the company. Participant contributions are always 100% vested from day one. Employer contributions vest according to the plan's vesting schedule — common schedules include immediate (100% vested right away), graded (e.g., 20% per year over 5 years), and cliff (e.g., 0% until 3 years of service, then 100%). The vested percentage determines how much of the account balance the participant can take with them when they leave.
The portion of the account balance that is eligible for distribution based on vesting percentage.

An electronic form used to submit a distribution request when portal submission is not possible (for example, MFA is not enrolled or the participant cannot log in). ForUsAll provides this form to the participant directly via a secure RightSignature link, after eligibility is confirmed.
The amount of tax that is withheld from a cash distribution to the participant.
An IRS tax form sent to the participant by January 31 of the following year to report distributions from retirement plans, including both cash distributions and rollovers.
A penalty that is applied to a distribution if the participant is under 59 1/2 years old.

The remaining unpaid amount on a 401(k) loan at the time of a termination distribution. If not repaid in full, the outstanding balance is treated as a taxable distribution and may incur an additional 10% IRS early withdrawal penalty if the participant is under 59 1/2.
For the benefit of; text that will automatically appear in paperwork and should not be manually entered in the Financial Institution field.
A routing number used for wire transfers to identify the receiving institution.
An account number for the participant's IRA or Roth IRA that must be entered correctly for wire rollovers.
A distribution reason used when a participant's employment has ended. This option is selected in the ForUsAll participant portal to initiate a termination distribution request.
The standard 401(k) termination distribution request flow used when a participant is Terminated and has a termination date on file.

A participant whose employment has ended, has a termination date on file, has eligibility status Terminated, and whose 401(k) account will be processed according to the termination distribution rules.
Official date recorded in the system indicating when a participant's employment ended.
The organization that maintains plan records and processes transactions such as distributions.
The area in the ForUsAll participant portal where a participant can initiate and submit distribution requests.
The total amount of money in a participant's 401(k) account that they own outright and can withdraw or roll over upon termination of employment.
The online account access point where participants can log in and submit a standard termination distribution request.

must_not: Do not state that unvested funds can be distributed; only vested balances are eligible.
Do not promise exact delivery dates; use the stated approximate timelines only.
Do not guarantee whether state withholding will apply or specify state withholding amounts.
Do not claim the wire fee can be refunded; the wire fee is non-refundable.

Do not claim where or how to access any document other than the portal URL, the RightSignature electronic form link, and contact methods explicitly provided in this article. The RightSignature electronic form link is shared directly with the participant once eligibility is confirmed, always with the note that it is only for participants who have problems with the website or cannot log in.
Do not claim that ForUsAll will help complete all required fields on this form.
Do not disclose account balances or vesting percentages, or any other sensitive information.
Do not claim that wire and check instructions are the same; many financial institutions have different details for wires versus ACH.
Do not promise that the rollover or distribution will be processed faster than the stated typical timelines.
Do not promise that ForUsAll will complete the process for the participant; they must enter the information themselves in the portal.
Do not provide processing timelines, delivery timelines, or confirmation timing that are not stated.
Do not assert eligibility requirements beyond terminated status and having a termination date on file.
Do not instruct the participant to contact the recordkeeper directly; the article directs participants to the ForUsAll portal or ForUsAll Support.
Do not state that unvested funds can be distributed under any scenario; only vested balances are eligible.
Do not tell a participant that an outstanding loan can be ignored during the termination distribution process; unpaid loan balances have tax and penalty consequences.

Do not offer hardship withdrawal, 401(k) loan, or in-service distribution when the participant explicitly states they have separated from employment (resigned, fired, no longer works there), even if the system Eligibility Status shows 'Active'. Escalate to verify the termination instead.
Do not offer, mention, or price OverNight Check delivery when describing the participant portal (website) process; overnight delivery cannot be requested there.
Do not quote $35 as the overnight check fee. The OverNight Check fee is $50; the $35 fee is the wire fee.
Do not present the RightSignature electronic form as the default, faster, or preferred submission route; it is shared only as a fallback for website or login problems.
Do not include ACH, 20% cash withholding, or cash-only penalty language in a pure direct-rollover response.
Do not promise how crypto-window holdings will transfer or be liquidated; this article does not define that treatment.
must_do_if_unsure: Advise the participant to contact ForUsAll Support if vesting percentages or account sources appear incorrect.

Once eligibility is confirmed, always include the RightSignature electronic form link in the response with a clear note that it is only for participants who have problems with the website or cannot log in (for example, MFA is not enrolled), rather than routing them to Support to obtain it.
Advise the participant to contact ForUsAll Support if employment separation status appears uncertain or not reflected in the portal options.
Advise the participant to contact ForUsAll Support if they are unsure about the information needed to complete the form.
Direct the participant to contact ForUsAll Support at help@forusall.com or 844-401-2253 if they are unsure which distribution type to select.

Instruct the participant to verify wire or check details directly with the receiving institution when the participant is uncertain about routing numbers, account numbers, subaccount numbers, or intermediary bank information.
If eligibility status Terminated is not on file or a termination date is not on file, do not confirm eligibility; request or retrieve the missing information using the appropriate source.
If the participant reports they submitted a request but the status is unknown, do not confirm completion or closure; request or retrieve the request status using the appropriate source.
If the participant asks when they will receive a confirmation and timing is not stated, do not estimate; request or retrieve the status/confirmation details using the appropriate source.

If the participant cannot locate the Loans & Distributions section or the Separation of Service reason in the portal, do not assume their portal view; provide the standard navigation steps and direct them to Support if it still does not appear or they state they cannot log in.
Advise the participant to contact ForUsAll Support if employment separation status appears uncertain or not reflected in the portal options.
If the participant mentions an outstanding loan, advise them to contact ForUsAll Support to discuss loan repayment options before initiating the distribution.
If the participant's last payroll date is fewer than 7 business days ago, advise them to wait before submitting to avoid missing funds and the need for a second distribution request.

If the participant says they have separated but the system shows Eligibility Status 'Active', request their termination/separation date, explain the system is out of sync and we will review it internally, and escalate to Support before offering any active-employee-only option.
If Crypto Enrollment is active or crypto holdings are mentioned, contact ForUsAll Support before submission rather than assuming liquidation or transfer behavior.
